subject: Clarify Ariba registration & MSA carve-outs for Capital Health onboarding
messages:
From: Capital Health Procurement <procure@capitalhealth.org>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: vendor.onboarding@capitalhealth.org
Date: Thu, 22 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify vendor registration fields + MSA carve-outs for Redwood

Hi Jordan,

Thanks for taking the call earlier. We're starting Redwood's vendor onboarding in Ariba and have two blockers before we can activate purchase orders:

1) MSA redline: Legal flagged two carve-outs (data residency & subprocessing) that your team proposed. Can you confirm whether Redwood will accept a narrow carve-out limited to (i) logs/telemetry retention for 30 days, and (ii) subprocessors listed in Sched A?

2) Ariba registration: our portal requires a supplier tax ID, preferred remit-to banking fields, and a required vendor classification code (we need a 6-digit NAICS-equivalent). Current vendor form doesn't map Redwood's fields cleanly — please send the exact field names we should populate so our onboarding team can pass to Ariba.

We also attached a short onboarding checklist from Capital Health (see referenced filename below) — happy to sync if it's easier. Targeting PO issuance by 11/02, so timing is tight.

Thanks,
Grace L. (on behalf of Procurement)
Grace Lin

Capital Health
procure@capitalhealth.org

Hi Grace — thanks for the clear note and timeline. Quick responses below and looping in Marissa (legal) for the MSA carve questions and Kimberly for Ariba-specific mappings.

- MSA carve-outs: Jordan here — short answer: we can accept a limited telemetry retention window and a narrow subprocessors list, but need legal to confirm precise language. Marissa, can you review the two points below and propose redline language we can accept?

- Ariba fields: Kimberly, can you confirm the exact field names Capital's onboarding team should use for Redwood (tax id, remit account format, and the 6-digit classification)? Our usual export has columns labeled: vendor_name, legal_name, tax_id, remit_account_iban, remit_country, primary_product_code. If we need a different column name or format we'll export a dedicated CSV.

Grace — propose a short 30-minute sync tomorrow (10/23) to finalize. If you prefer asynchronous, we'll send the redline and a vendor CSV sample by EOD today.

Subject: Re: Clarify vendor registration fields + MSA carve-outs for Redwood

Hi all — I reviewed the proposed carve-outs and drafted language that should be acceptable to both sides with minimal exposure for Redwood. Summary of redline points: 

1) Telemetry/logs retention: Redwood agrees to retain only operational telemetry (performance/health metrics and anonymized request telemetry) for a maximum of 30 days by default. Any retention beyond 30 days will require a documented business justification and mutual written agreement.

2) Subprocessors: Redwood will list all authorized subprocessors in Schedule A and will notify Capital Health within 30 days of material changes. For time-sensitive subprocessors used solely for transient delivery optimizations (CDN, ephemeral tracing for performance debugging) Redwood will provide a limited exception process with prior notice.

3) Liability & indemnity: Proposed to keep the standard mutual limitation-of-liability clause but add an explicit carve for breach resulting from Redwood's gross negligence or willful misconduct.

I've attached a redline and a one-page summary for your legal ops team to review. If this is acceptable, Jordan — we should propose these language changes as tracked redlines in the MSA and provide an order form template with required PO fields called out (tax id, remit IBAN, vendor class code).

Attachments: Capital_Health_MSA_redline.docx, redline_summary.txt

Marissa Cole
Head of Legal Operations
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
